findings.source: Mathematics Stack Exchange — Expected number of intersection points when n random chords are drawn in a circle
findings.relationship: Uses four endpoints, notes the three pairings are equiprobable, one crosses, and obtains n(n-1)/6.
findings.notes: The sampling description is not literally 'a uniform perfect matching of fixed seats', but the decisive local law and expected value are exactly the frozen candidate's mechanism.

findings.source: Hüseyin Acan, On a uniformly random chord diagram and its intersection graph, Discrete Mathematics 340 (2017)
findings.relationship: Uses the exact story-stripped object: a uniformly random chord diagram / perfect matching of cyclic endpoints, and places crossing statistics in established literature.
findings.notes: Together with the direct elementary solution above, this removes any defensible novelty claim for the frozen problem.

coverage_assessment.why_reasonably_strong_or_not: The exact model is a standard random chord diagram and the exact mean/proof already appears publicly in elementary form; additional source classes cannot restore novelty.

classification_rationale: The frozen problem is the standard expected crossing count for a uniformly random chord diagram. The answer n(n-1)/6 and the four-endpoint, one-of-three-pairings proof are already public. A different ribbon story is cosmetic.
follow_up_required: Do not select. Any salvage would need a materially different statistic or constrained matching model; merely changing the story is not salvage.
